answer: Ask what a clone farm cannot buy in bulk, and the answer points at Proof of presence via Wi-Fi BSSID history. It requires a router history that matches a real home, so the river of scaling up is a queue of real-world chores. Scale stops helping the attacker here. Ten clones need ten separate proofs, each with its own a router history that matches a real home, and the timber grows linearly while the reward per clone stays flat. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The fable is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
